name: Progressive Osseous Heteroplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Progressive Osseous Heteroplasia

criteria.description: Progressive heterotopic ossification involving skin, subcutaneous, and deep connective tissues
Onset of heterotopic ossification during infancy or early childhood
Identification of inactivating mutations in the GNAS gene
Radiographic absence of endochondral bone formation in heterotopic lesions
Exclusion of fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva and other related disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive heterotopic ossification in skin and deep connective tissues with onset in infancy or early childhood, supported by clinical and radiographic findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for GNAS mutations can support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive heterotopic ossification in dermis and subcutaneous tissues
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic progressive bone formation outside the normal skeleton
searchTerms: progressive abnormal bone growth under skin
increasing bone formation in skin layers
hardening of skin due to bone growth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Deep connective tissue ossification extending into skeletal muscle
pathognomonic.notes: Distinguishes POH from other superficial ossification disorders
searchTerms: abnormal bone formation in connective tissue and muscle

pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents in infancy or early childhood
searchTerms: early hard skin patches with bone formation
skin plaques turning to bone in childhood

common.symptomName: Restricted joint mobility due to heterotopic bone
common.notes: Progressive limitation of movement in affected areas
searchTerms: stiff joints due to extra bone
limited joint movement from bone growth

common.symptomName: Subcutaneous nodules or plaques palpable under the skin
common.notes: Firm ossified nodules often detected on physical exam
searchTerms: lumps or hard plaques under skin

common.symptomName: Pain or tenderness over ossified lesions
common.notes: Variable pain associated with active ossification
searchTerms: discomfort on touch of bone plaques

common.symptomName: Skin dimpling or atrophy over ossified areas
common.notes: Secondary skin changes due to underlying ossification
searchTerms: skin dimpling or thinning over bone growth
skin shrinking or scarring above ossified spots

occasional.symptomName: Superficial ossification limited to dermis without deep extension
occasional.notes: May represent early or mild disease
searchTerms: bone formation limited to skin surface

occasional.symptomName: Mild limb deformities due to heterotopic bone
occasional.notes: Deformities secondary to ossification and joint restriction
searchTerms: mild limb deformities from extra bone
minor limb abnormalities due to bone growth

occasional.symptomName: Localized skin erythema or inflammation preceding ossification
occasional.notes: Inflammatory signs may precede ossification episodes
searchTerms: redness or swelling before bone growth

occasional.notes: Due to restricted movement from ossification

rare.symptomName: Heterotopic ossification involving deeper skeletal structures
rare.notes: Rare extension beyond connective tissues into bone
searchTerms: abnormal bone formation in deep skeletal tissues

rare.symptomName: Secondary skin ulceration over ossified plaques
rare.notes: Ulceration due to skin compromise over bony lesions
searchTerms: open sores on ossified skin areas

rare.symptomName: Mild constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: mild general symptoms like low-grade fever

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biomarkers identified
imaging: Radiographs showing heterotopic ossification in dermis, subcutaneous tissue, and deep connective tissues without endochondral ossification
CT or MRI may delineate extent of ossification
genetic: Inactivating mutations in GNAS gene (encoding Gs alpha protein)
other: Histopathology reveals intramembranous ossification in affected tissues

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of congenital malformations of the great toes
Localized ossification limited to skin without progression into deep tissues
No progressive deep connective tissue involvement

redFlags: Rapid progression of heterotopic ossification causing severe joint ankylosis
Early onset of ossification in infancy
Involvement of deep connective tissues and skeletal muscle
references: Kaplan FS, Shore EM. Progressive Osseous Heteroplasia. GeneReviews. 2020.
Pignolo RJ, Shore EM, Kaplan FS. Fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva: clinical and genetic aspects. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2011.
